why: A ships the same wrap but catches the production trap that makes B's migration a no-op in the built image (the Dockerfile copies only llmcord.py and config.yaml, so router_runtime.py would be absent and the import guard would silently degrade), and is far more honest about what translation costs (extra_headers, extra_query, dropped sampling params) where B writes 'loses: nothing'. On system judgment A also sweeps more of the Router surface with reasons — Flex measured rather than assumed, fallbacks built and tested, a key-level spend cap plus a per-user rate limit for a bot shipping allow_dms with an empty allowlist, and explicit, argued rejections of Switchyard, Jev and service_tier=default — whereas B's two genuinely deeper items (catalog-driven capabilities, provider consolidation) don't offset leaving spend entirely unbounded.
A_best: Caught that the Dockerfile would have shipped an image without the runtime, silently reverting the migration — plus the spend-cap/rate-limit pairing that names the actual financial exposure (public bot, allow_dms, empty allowlist, no cooldown, 128k unbounded output) and fixes it at both the key and the app.
B_best: i6 and i7 are the only true rework proposals in either report and both are correct and specific: replacing the VISION_MODEL_TAGS substring heuristic with Router's catalog capabilities (caught live when gpt-6-luna would have been treated as text-only), and a per-block analysis of consolidating openrouter/x-ai onto the one key, including which ids map natively and why Gemini (BYOK) and the local servers must not move.
A_worst: Declined host consolidation as 'a customer decision', so after shipping, most of the bot's selectable models still bypass the gateway entirely — the one place B reached further — and A keeps the name-substring vision heuristic rather than questioning it.
B_worst: 'loses: nothing' on m1 is wrong for the same runtime whose translation losses A enumerates, the Dockerfile omission means the migration would not actually be in the deployed image, and for a bot anyone can DM there is no spend cap, no rate limit, and no mention of shadow models, Jev or Switchyard.
